findings.description: The bucket is explicitly noted and configured to be publicly accessible, with no ACL restricting access, allowing unauthenticated users to read/write objects such as the customer-master.xlsx file stored in it.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so objects including sensitive customer data are stored unencrypted at rest.
The bucket has no logging configuration, making it impossible to audit access to sensitive data, compounding the impact of the public exposure.
Versioning is not enabled, so accidental or malicious deletion/overwrite of objects (facilitated by force_destroy and public access) cannot be recovered from.
A customer master data file (customer-master.xlsx) is uploaded into the aws_s3_bucket.data bucket, which is public and unencrypted, directly exposing sensitive customer data to unauthorized access.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined for this bucket holding financial data, leaving it unencrypted at rest despite having a private ACL.
The bucket lacks an access logging configuration, preventing audit visibility into access of sensitive financial data.
Versioning is not enabled on this financial data bucket, and force_destroy is set to true, increasing risk of irreversible data loss.

The bucket does not define a server_side_encryption_configuration block, meaning objects stored in it are not encrypted at rest by default, risking exposure of sensitive data if underlying storage or backups are compromised.
The bucket has no logging block configured, so there is no audit trail of access requests, hampering detection of unauthorized access to potentially sensitive operations data.

The bucket does not define a server_side_encryption_configuration block, so data stored in it is not encrypted at rest, exposing potentially sensitive data-science datasets to risk if storage is compromised.
